stem: Two otherwise matched experimental groups establish an antibody response to the same antigen. Investigators then selectively remove memory B cells from group X before repeat exposure, leaving group Y unchanged. Which early recall-response pattern most directly supports a contribution from those cells?

options.label: A
options.text: Unchanged cell expansion and antibody production between groups
options.explanation: An unchanged early response would fail to show the contribution being tested. The proposed mechanism predicts a weaker accelerated recall component after selective memory-cell removal.
options.misconception: Treats removal of the proposed recall population as producing no change in either early readout.

options.label: B
options.text: Less rapid cell expansion and antibody production in X
options.explanation: Memory B cells support rapid proliferation and antibody production after re-exposure. Selective removal predicts loss of that accelerated component compared with the otherwise matched group.
options.misconception: No misconception: Removing memory B cells should reduce the accelerated expansion and antibody response.

options.label: C
options.text: More rapid cell expansion and antibody production in X
options.explanation: This reverses the proposed memory-cell contribution. Removing the population responsible for accelerated recall should not enhance the same early proliferation and antibody-production response.
options.misconception: Predicts that removing the cells supporting rapid recall accelerates both recall readouts.

options.label: D
options.text: Less rapid cell expansion but greater antibody production in X
options.explanation: Reduced expansion fits removal of the memory population, but greater early antibody production does not follow from the same proposed loss of accelerated recall function.
options.misconception: Combines reduced expansion with increased antibody output despite the proposed loss of accelerated recall.

options.label: E
options.text: More rapid cell expansion but lower antibody production in X
options.explanation: Lower antibody output fits an impaired recall response, but increased expansion reverses the expected effect on the depleted population. Both readouts should reflect reduced acceleration.
options.misconception: Combines reduced antibody output with increased expansion despite depletion of the recall population.

context: Learning objective: Test memory B-cell function using a matched repeat-exposure comparison. Removing those cells targets the accelerated proliferation and antibody production of the recall response.
